correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the array and inverse induction from the proper Abelian-border definition. Subtracting both equal Parikh vectors from the full vector interchanges lengths j and i-j, even when the blocks overlap. Write d=2^nu2(i). If i=d, the final ruler letter first occurs there, so all proper suffixes contain a letter absent from all proper prefixes. If i>d, then nu2(i-d+j)=nu2(j) for 1<=j<d by divisibility, and the terminal valuation equals nu2(d); the length-d blocks are identical. Every shorter positive suffix length contains the terminal letter which is not yet in the matching prefix, so the longest Abelian border has length i-d. Conversely, assume the earlier letters of a realizing word are already identified by valuation. At i=2^k, reusing the letter at level s<k would make the first and last length-2^s blocks identical by the valuation identity, contrary to the required zero. This forces a new letter. At nonpowers of two, the length-d Abelian border is prescribed by complementarity, and the known length-(d-1) parts agree letter-for-letter, leaving only the terminal letter to match the prefix's level-nu2(i) letter. This also works at d=1 (empty known blocks); n=1 is immediate. Exactly the levels 0 to floor(log2 n) occur, giving necessity and sufficiency of the claimed alphabet size for this family and only a lower bound on the worst-case M(n). Inspected frozen RESULT.md lines 35–66, VERIFICATION.md and verify.py. The finite restricted-growth checks are corroborative; the all-alphabet and all-length claims follow from the reconstruction, not from executing the supplied script, which was not run.

evidence: The Habib–Shamil–Rahman inverse propositions concern binary words; their §4 exhibits larger-alphabet non-injectivity. Thus they give uniqueness restricted to binary realizations of the short binary instances, not rigidity against arbitrary alphabets.

The indexed finite ternary result counts arrays and describes ambiguity, not an arbitrary-alphabet inverse theorem. The Abelian bordered-word counting paper counts individual words with or without borders, not full array realizations.

evidence: The known duality yields the existence of a length-d Abelian border from a prescribed longest border i-d but does not identify its letters. Binary reconstruction and fixed-ternary computation are not estimates of the minimum across all realizing alphabets.
The ruler morphism constructs one word, not the absence of other words yielding its array.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The surviving inverse argument forces fresh letters at exactly the powers of two and inductively recovers the remaining letters by Parikh cancellation. Neither the standard morphism nor the binary inverse theorem supplies those arbitrary-alphabet constraints.

evidence: Habib–Shamil–Rahman and the survey identify the shortest/longest proper Abelian-border duality, so the formulation using shortest positive border 2^nu2(i) when it exists is equivalent.
Berera et al. identify the same ruler sequence as the fixed point of rho(n)=0(n+1), but study a different, square-free-word problem.
Ordinary exact borders and longest Abelian borders are not interchangeable: the ruler prefix 010 has longest exact border one and longest Abelian border two.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Known alternative descriptions of the ruler sequence and the border-length duality are credited. They do not say that the entire vector of Abelian-border observations forces the sequence's equality pattern for any alphabet.

value.rationale: The inverse problem is not injective over larger alphabets, and introducing many letters in one example word alone would not rule out a small-alphabet representative. This natural dyadic family proves rigidity where the general inverse fails and supplies an explicit logarithmic obstruction to any fixed universal alphabet. It separates the exact minimum for the family from the still broader extremal function M(n).
